intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami (flower viewing) tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees, enjoy street food stalls, and witness traditional lantern-lit evening viewing. A perfect family cultural immersion that captures the heart of Japanese spring.

experiences.name: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Explore a mesmerizing world of immersive, interactive digital art installations spread across multiple rooms. Children and adults alike are captivated by the flowing light displays, interactive projections, and dreamlike environments. A uniquely Japanese fusion of technology and art that the whole family will remember.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through Tokyo's legendary outer market sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha sweets, and street snacks. Engage with friendly vendors, learn about Japanese food culture, and enjoy a hands-on culinary adventure that introduces the whole family to authentic Japanese flavors.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo forest of Arashiyama, then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will love hand-feeding the monkeys while parents enjoy panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a rickshaw ride along the scenic Oi River for a full cultural and nature experience.

experiences.name: Traditional Samurai and Ninja Experience
experiences.description: Dress the whole family in authentic samurai armor or ninja costumes and learn basic sword techniques and ninja skills from trained instructors. This hands-on cultural workshop offers a thrilling and educational window into feudal Japanese history. Children especially love the ninja throwing star and stealth training activities.
experiences.location: Samurai Kembu Theater, Higashiyama district, Kyoto

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami (flower viewing) tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees, enjoy street food stalls, and witness traditional lantern-lit evening viewing. A perfect family cultural immersion that captures the heart of Japanese spring.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage. Take the Airport Limousine Bus or train to your accommodation (Aegean Bliss Resort). Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to recover from jet lag.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable meal at the airport — try a bowl of ramen or udon at one of the airport food stalls (approx. ¥800–¥1,200). Convenience stores like 7-Eleven or FamilyMart near the hotel are great for late-night budget snacks.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase an IC card (Suica or Pasmo) at the airport for easy and discounted public transit throughout your trip. Also consider picking up a pocket WiFi or SIM card at the airport for navigation.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag with a slow morning. Walk along the beachfront near the resort to enjoy the fresh air and spring scenery. Visit a nearby convenience store (7-Eleven or Lawson) for a classic Japanese breakfast — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and green tea for under ¥500.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local neighborhood on foot. Visit a nearby Shinto shrine or local temple to ease into Japanese culture. Look for any local cherry blossom trees in bloom along the streets or in small parks — April is peak season!
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local izakaya (Japanese gastropub) near the resort for dinner. Order small shared plates like edamame, karaage (fried chicken), and yakitori skewers. Budget-friendly and a great cultural experience for the whole family.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast (onigiri, boiled egg, green tea) — approx. ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Nearby ramen shop or soba noodle restaurant — approx. ¥700–¥1,000 per person
meals.dinner: Local izakaya — approx. ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today — jet lag is real! Staying close to the hotel helps the family adjust. Check local cherry blossom forecast apps like Tenki.jp for peak bloom updates.

day_by_day.morning: Take a train to Kyoto and head straight to Maruyama Park for the iconic Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. Witness the famous weeping cherry tree in full bloom. Arrive early (by 9:00 AM) to enjoy it before crowds build up. Bring a picnic blanket and snacks from a convenience store for an authentic hanami picnic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from Maruyama Park to the nearby Yasaka Shrine (free entry) and stroll through the charming Higashiyama District. Explore the stone-paved Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes lined with traditional shops and sakura trees. Browse affordable souvenirs like fans, chopsticks, and tenugui towels.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Stop at a local kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) restaurant for a fun, family-friendly, budget dinner — plates start at ¥100–¥150 each.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel breakfast — approx. ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Hanami picnic in Maruyama Park — buy onigiri, sandwiches, and snacks from a convenience store for ¥500–¥800 per person
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi restaurant — approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Maruyama Park is free to enter. Wear comfortable walking shoes — Higashiyama involves cobblestone paths and gentle hills. Bring a reusable bag for picnic supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine in Kyoto — free entry! Walk through the iconic thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up the mountain. The lower trail takes about 30–45 minutes and is manageable for families with children. Go early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nishiki Market — Kyoto's famous narrow covered market street nicknamed 'Kyoto's Kitchen.' Sample street food like tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelet), pickled vegetables, and fresh tofu for very affordable prices. Great cultural and culinary experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Gion District at dusk — the historic geisha district is magical in the evening light. Walk along Hanamikoji Street and look for maiko (apprentice geisha). Dinner at a nearby teishoku (set meal) restaurant for a balanced, affordable Japanese meal.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — approx. ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Street food snacks at Nishiki Market — approx. ¥600–¥1,000 per person
meals.dinner: Teishoku set meal restaurant in Gion — approx. ¥900–¥1,400 per person

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free and open 24 hours. Nishiki Market closes around 6 PM so plan accordingly. Gion evening walks are free — just be respectful of locals and do not photograph geisha without permission.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara — easily accessible by train from Kyoto (approx. 45 minutes, ~¥720 one way). Visit Nara Park where hundreds of free-roaming deer bow to visitors for shika senbei (deer crackers, ¥200/pack). Kids absolutely love this! Walk to the massive Todai-ji Temple housing the giant bronze Buddha (entry ¥600 adults, ¥300 children).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Kasuga Taisha Shrine (free outer grounds) and enjoy the lantern-lined forested paths. Explore the charming Naramachi historic merchant district with free-entry preserved townhouses and small craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto or your resort area by train. Dinner at a yoshoku (Western-Japanese fusion) family restaurant chain like Gusto or Joyfull — very budget-friendly with kids' menus available.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store — approx. ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Nara local restaurant — try kakinoha-zushi (persimmon leaf sushi), a Nara specialty — approx. ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Family restaurant chain — approx. ¥700–¥1,200 per person

day_by_day.notes: Buy a round-trip train ticket to save time. Deer crackers are sold near the park entrance. Keep bags zipped — deer are friendly but curious and may nibble on belongings!

day_by_day.morning: Visit Arashiyama in western Kyoto. Walk through the famous Bamboo Grove (free) — one of Japan's most photographed spots. Explore the serene Tenryu-ji Temple gardens (¥500 garden entry) with stunning cherry blossom views over the pond.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent bikes near Arashiyama station (approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500/day) and cycle along the Hozu River through the scenic countryside. Visit Jojakko-ji Temple (¥400 entry) — a hidden gem with beautiful moss gardens and fewer crowds. Great for family photos among the sakura.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Cook a simple meal using ingredients from a local supermarket (Aeon, Life, or Seiyu) — bento boxes, pre-made sushi, and miso soup packets are excellent budget options and a fun cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or convenience store — approx. ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Arashiyama tofu cuisine restaurant or noodle shop — approx. ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Supermarket bento and prepared foods — approx. ¥500–¥800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama is best visited on a weekday morning to avoid crowds. The bamboo grove is free but very popular — arrive before 8:30 AM for the best experience and photos.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Osaka by train (approx. 15–20 minutes from Kyoto, ~¥560). Visit Osaka Castle Park — the castle grounds and park are free to walk around and stunning with late-season cherry blossoms. Castle interior entry is ¥600 per adult and worth it for the panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Dotonbori — Osaka's vibrant entertainment and food district. Walk along the neon-lit canal, see the famous Glico Running Man sign, and sample Osaka's street food culture. Must-try: takoyaki (octopus balls, ¥500–¥700 for 8 pieces) and okonomiyaki (savory pancake, ¥800–¥1,200).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Shinsaibashi shopping arcade for budget souvenir shopping. Dinner at a standing sushi bar (tachigui-zushi) or a local kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers) restaurant — quintessential Osaka budget dining.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store — approx. ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Dotonbori street food — takoyaki, taiyaki, and crepes — approx. ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Kushikatsu restaurant or standing sushi bar — approx. ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is known as 'Japan's kitchen' — food here is world-class and very affordable. Use the IC card for seamless train travel between cities. Dotonbori is very lively at night — great for family evening walks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Universal Studios Japan (USJ) in Osaka — a perfect family activity day! Purchase tickets in advance online for discounts (approx. ¥8,600–¥9,800 adults, ¥5,600–¥6,100 children). Arrive at opening time (usually 9:00 AM) to beat queues. Highlights: Super Nintendo World, The Wizarding World of Harry Potter, and Minion Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying USJ — afternoon shows and parades are a highlight. Take advantage of the Express Pass for popular rides if budget allows, or use the single rider option to save time for free.
day_by_day.evening: Exit USJ by 6:00–7:00 PM. Grab dinner near Universal City station — affordable chain restaurants and food courts available. Return to resort by train.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before USJ — approx. ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: USJ food court or themed restaurant (budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person inside the park)
meals.dinner: Restaurant near Universal City station — approx. ¥800–¥1,200 per person

day_by_day.notes: USJ is the biggest splurge of the trip but absolutely worth it for families. Book tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance online for better prices. Bring refillable water bottles to save on drinks inside the park.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning near the resort — enjoy the beachfront scenery and take a leisurely walk. Visit a local morning market or farmers market if available nearby. Pick up fresh local produce, Japanese sweets (wagashi), and snacks as take-home gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby onsen (hot spring bath) facility — a quintessential Japanese cultural experience. Many public sento bathhouses charge only ¥400–¥800 per person. Look for a family-friendly onsen with indoor and outdoor baths. This is deeply relaxing and culturally immersive.
day_by_day.evening: Final special dinner — treat the family to a shabu-shabu or sukiyaki all-you-can-eat restaurant (approx. ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person). A memorable and interactive dining experience where you cook thin slices of meat and vegetables in broth at your table.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or convenience store — approx. ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Local teishoku restaurant or udon shop — approx. ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: All-you-can-eat shabu-shabu or sukiyaki — approx. ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check onsen rules in advance — some facilities do not allow guests with tattoos. Most onsens provide towels for a small fee or you can bring your own. Children are welcome at most public baths.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and enjoy a final Japanese breakfast — visit a nearby kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) for morning toast with butter and jam, a boiled egg, and coffee (approx. ¥400–¥700). Pack bags and check out of the resort. Do a final souvenir sweep at a 100-yen shop (Daiso) for affordable gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and immigration. Browse duty-free shops for last-minute Japanese snacks, sake, and cosmetics. Spend remaining yen on airport snacks or gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Japan with wonderful memories of cherry blossoms, culture, and family adventures!

meals.breakfast: Kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) — approx. ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Airport food court or terminal restaurant — approx. ¥900–¥1,400
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Return your IC card (Suica/Pasmo) at the airport for a refund of the ¥500 deposit plus remaining balance. Keep all receipts for tax-free shopping refunds at the airport. Japan's consumption tax (10%) can be refunded on purchases over ¥5,000 at tax-free counters.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at the airport's 24-hour ramen or soba counter (¥800–¥1,200 per person) before or after baggage claim. Convenience stores like 7-Eleven or FamilyMart at the airport are also excellent for onigiri, sandwiches, and hot drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day only. Do not book any tours or activities for this day. Prioritize rest to combat jet lag. Set out your next-day essentials before sleeping. Consider purchasing a Suica/Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast to recover from jet lag. Take a relaxing morning stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to soak in the coastal scenery and get oriented with the local surroundings. Visit a nearby convenience store or local café to pick up snacks and essentials for the trip ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest city center for a gentle orientation walk. Explore a local shopping street (shotengai) or covered arcade to browse souvenirs, pick up travel accessories, and get a feel for Japanese urban life. Visit a nearby shrine or temple for a calm cultural introduction — perfect for families. Look for any local cherry blossom trees in bloom along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed family dinner at a mid-range izakaya (Japanese gastropub) near the hotel. Try shared dishes like karaage (fried chicken), edamame, gyoza, and grilled skewers. Return to the hotel early to rest and prepare for a full day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy Japanese staples like miso soup, steamed rice, grilled fish, and pickles alongside Western options (included or ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a local café or convenience store near the hotel — try onigiri sets, sandwiches, or a simple teishoku (set meal) for ¥600–¥1,200.
meals.dinner: Family-friendly izakaya near the hotel — budget approximately ¥2,000–¥3,500 per adult, ¥800–¥1,200 for children. Look for restaurants with picture menus for easy ordering.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 2 light and flexible to allow for jet lag recovery. Japan operates on a very different time zone, and pushing too hard on Day 2 can exhaust the family. Hydrate well and try to stay awake until at least 9 PM local time to reset your body clock.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Tokyo for a full day of exploration. Start the morning with the iconic Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — wander through Tokyo's legendary outer market sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), fresh seafood, and street snacks. This is a fantastic sensory experience for the whole family and a wonderful introduction to Japanese food culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market tour, head to the TeamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum for an awe-inspiring afternoon. Explore mesmerizing immersive and interactive digital art installations spread across multiple rooms. Children and adults alike will be captivated by the light, sound, and movement experiences. Book tickets in advance as this attraction sells out quickly.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Odaiba waterfront area near TeamLab for dinner and evening entertainment. Walk along the waterfront promenade with views of the Rainbow Bridge and Tokyo skyline illuminated at night. Browse the DiverCity Tokyo Plaza for dinner options ranging from ramen to family restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure, or grab a quick breakfast at Tsukiji market upon arrival — fresh tuna sushi, tamagoyaki on a stick, and matcha tea for ¥1,000–¥1,800 per person.
meals.lunch: Enjoy lunch as part of the Tsukiji Outer Market experience — graze on market stalls featuring fresh seafood bowls (kaisen-don), grilled scallops, and crab legs. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a family restaurant in Odaiba — try Kua'Aina for burgers, a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) chain, or a tonkatsu restaurant. Budget ¥1,800–¥3,000 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: TeamLab Borderless tickets must be booked online in advance at teamlab.art — they frequently sell out weeks ahead, especially on weekends. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Tsukiji. The market is best experienced between 9–11 AM before crowds peak. Allow 2–3 hours for TeamLab.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning exploring Tokyo's family-friendly Ueno Park, which is one of the best cherry blossom viewing spots in the city. In mid-April, late-blooming varieties may still be showing color. Walk the park's main promenade lined with sakura trees, visit the Toshogu Shrine, and enjoy the festive hanami atmosphere with local families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ueno Zoo — Japan's oldest zoo and a fantastic family activity. See giant pandas, polar bears, gorillas, and many more animals. Alternatively, explore the Tokyo National Museum within Ueno Park for an introduction to Japanese art, samurai armor, and cultural artifacts. Both options are within easy walking distance of each other.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Asakusa for an enchanting evening stroll through one of Tokyo's most historic neighborhoods. Walk the iconic Nakamise shopping street leading to Senso-ji Temple, which is beautifully lit up at night. Browse traditional craft shops for omiyage (souvenirs) and try ningyo-yaki (small cakes shaped like dolls) from street vendors.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near the hotel serving morning sets with toast, egg, and coffee for ¥500–¥900.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch in Ueno Park — pick up bento boxes and drinks from a nearby convenience store or the park's food stalls. Budget ¥800–¥1,500 per person. Eating outdoors under the cherry blossoms is a quintessential hanami experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Asakusa at a traditional tempura or sukiyaki restaurant. Try Daikokuya Tempura (a famous local institution) or a nearby family restaurant with a varied menu. Budget ¥2,000–¥3,500 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Ueno Park can be very crowded on weekends during cherry blossom season — arrive early (before 9 AM) to secure a good spot. Ueno Zoo is closed on Mondays. Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa is open 24 hours, but the Nakamise shops close around 6–7 PM, so plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen (bullet train) from Tokyo to Kyoto — a smooth and exciting 2 hour 15 minute journey on the Tokaido Shinkansen. This is itself a memorable experience for families, especially catching views of Mount Fuji on clear days (look out the right side of the train heading west). Arrive in Kyoto and check into a day-use locker at Kyoto Station to store luggage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head directly to Arashiyama for the iconic Bamboo Grove experience. Walk through the towering green bamboo forest of Sagano, one of Japan's most photographed landscapes. Then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park to see Japanese macaques roaming freely with panoramic views of Kyoto below. This is a huge hit with families and children.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Arashiyama riverside area as the sun sets — stroll across Togetsukyo Bridge, browse artisan shops along the main street, and enjoy the peaceful atmosphere. Return to Kyoto city center for dinner in the Gion district, Kyoto's historic geisha quarter, where traditional machiya townhouses line the stone-paved streets.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at Tokyo Station's bakeries or food halls before boarding the Shinkansen — try a station bento (ekiben) or a croissant and coffee for ¥500–¥1,200.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Arashiyama at a tofu cuisine restaurant — Kyoto is famous for refined tofu dishes. Try yudofu (simmered tofu) set meals at a riverside restaurant for ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Gion at a mid-range kaiseki-inspired restaurant or a cozy ramen shop. Try Ippudo or Kyoto Ramen Koji for approachable, family-friendly options. Budget ¥1,800–¥3,000 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen tickets in advance through the JR Pass or at a JR ticket office — reserve seats for the family to sit together. Iwatayama Monkey Park requires a 20-minute uphill hike — wear comfortable shoes and carry water. Do not feed the monkeys outside the designated feeding area.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the magical Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park — Kyoto's most famous hanami destination. The park's iconic weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) is one of the most photographed trees in Japan. Arrive early to enjoy the serene atmosphere before crowds arrive. Walk through the park, take family photos, and embrace the traditional hanami spirit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Higashiyama district on foot — one of Kyoto's best-preserved historic neighborhoods. Walk the famous Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka stone-paved lanes lined with traditional wooden shops selling matcha sweets, ceramics, and textiles. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple perched dramatically on a hillside with sweeping city views.
day_by_day.evening: Participate in the Traditional Samurai and Ninja Experience — dress the whole family in authentic samurai armor or ninja costumes and learn basic sword techniques and ninja moves from experienced instructors. This is an unforgettable, hands-on cultural activity that children absolutely love. Many studios offer professional photo packages.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a local Kyoto café — try a traditional Kyoto-style morning set with rice porridge (okayu), pickles, and green tea.
meals.lunch: Lunch along Ninenzaka or Sannenzaka — try matcha soba noodles, yatsuhashi (Kyoto's famous cinnamon rice cake), or a bento from a local shop. Budget ¥1,200–¥2,000 per person.
meals.dinner: Celebrate the samurai experience with a festive dinner at a shabu-shabu or sukiyaki restaurant in central Kyoto. Cooking your own thinly sliced beef at the table is a fun, interactive family meal. Budget ¥3,000–¥4,500 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Maruyama Park is free to enter and open 24 hours. The weeping cherry tree is beautifully illuminated at night if you wish to return after the samurai experience. Book the Samurai and Ninja Experience in advance — popular studios include Samurai Kembu Theater and Kyoto Samurai & Ninja Museum. Sessions typically last 60–90 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha — Kyoto's famous shrine with thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up a forested mountain. Start early to beat the crowds and hike as far up the trail as the family is comfortable — even the lower section with its iconic tunnel of gates is spectacular. The full hike takes 2–3 hours but partial routes are equally rewarding.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Nishiki Market — Kyoto's narrow, covered 'Kitchen of Kyoto' market street. Sample pickled vegetables, fresh tofu, skewered seafood, sweet potato chips, and matcha-flavored everything. This is a wonderful cultural and culinary afternoon for curious families. Browse the stalls and pick up unique food souvenirs to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a peaceful evening stroll through the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi) — a canal-side walkway lined with cherry trees. In mid-April, late-blooming Yaezakura (double-petal cherry blossoms) may still be in flower. End the evening with a quiet dinner in the Nanzenji area.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before heading to Fushimi Inari — fuel up with a hearty meal for the morning hike.
meals.lunch: Graze through Nishiki Market for lunch — budget ¥1,000–¥1,800 per person sampling various stalls. Don't miss the fresh tamagoyaki, pickled plum onigiri, and hot skewered tofu.
meals.dinner: Dinner near the Philosopher's Path — try a cozy neighborhood restaurant serving Kyoto obanzai (traditional home-style small dishes). Budget ¥2,000–¥3,000 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is free to enter and open 24 hours. Arrive before 8 AM for the best photos without crowds. Wear sturdy walking shoes for the uneven stone steps. Nishiki Market is best visited between 10 AM and 5 PM — most stalls close by early evening.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nara — just 45 minutes from Kyoto by train. Start the morning at Nara Park where hundreds of freely roaming sacred deer will bow to you in exchange for shika senbei (deer crackers). Children will be delighted. Walk to the magnificent Todai-ji Temple housing Japan's largest bronze Buddha statue — a truly awe-inspiring sight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nara's Kasuga Taisha Grand Shrine, famous for its thousands of stone and bronze lanterns lining mossy forest paths. Walk through the serene Nara forests and enjoy the peaceful contrast to the busier city experiences. Browse the Naramachi historic merchant district for traditional crafts and local sweets before heading back to Kyoto.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto for a relaxing evening. Treat the family to a traditional Japanese bath experience (onsen or sento) at a local public bathhouse — a deeply cultural and refreshing activity after days of walking. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing for Nara.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Nara at a restaurant near Todai-ji — try kakinoha-zushi (sushi wrapped in persimmon leaves, a Nara specialty) or a set meal at a local restaurant. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person.
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner in Kyoto at a mid-range family restaurant or conveyor belt sushi — unwind after a full day of exploring. Budget ¥1,500–¥2,500 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Deer crackers (shika senbei) are sold at stalls throughout Nara Park for approximately ¥200 per bundle. Keep food items hidden in bags as the deer are persistent and will nudge or nibble at bags. Young children should be supervised closely around the deer. The Kintetsu Nara Line from Kyoto offers the most direct route.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Tokyo by Shinkansen for the final stretch of the trip. Upon arriving in Tokyo, head to the Shibuya and Harajuku area. Start with a walk through Yoyogi Park — a beloved local park with wide open lawns perfect for a relaxed morning. Check for any late-blooming cherry trees and enjoy the lively weekend atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Takeshita Street in Harajuku for a fun, colorful, and uniquely Japanese pop culture experience — try rainbow cotton candy, crepes, and browse quirky fashion boutiques. Then walk down the elegant Omotesando boulevard for window shopping and café stops. Visit the Kiddy Land toy store for an impressive selection of Japanese toys and character goods.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the famous Shibuya Crossing experience — stand on the second floor of the Starbucks overlooking the world's busiest pedestrian crossing for a spectacular view, especially at night. Explore the surrounding area and enjoy a final full Tokyo dinner at a restaurant of the family's choice.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Kyoto Station before boarding the Shinkansen — pick up an ekiben (station bento box) to enjoy on the train.
meals.lunch: Crepes and snacks along Takeshita Street for a fun, casual lunch — budget ¥800–¥1,500 per person grazing street food stalls.
meals.dinner: Celebratory family dinner in Shibuya — try a high-quality yakiniku (Japanese BBQ) restaurant where everyone grills their own meat at the table. Budget ¥3,000–¥4,500 per adult. Alternatively, explore the food floors of Shibuya Hikarie or Scramble Square for diverse options.

day_by_day.notes: Harajuku's Takeshita Street is very narrow and can become extremely crowded on Friday afternoons — visit before 3 PM if possible. The Shibuya Crossing Starbucks (Shibuya Tsutaya) does not take reservations — arrive early to secure a window seat. Keep valuables secure in crowded Shibuya.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and take a last stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to savor the coastal scenery. Pack and prepare for departure. Do a final souvenir run at a nearby Don Quijote (discount variety store) or airport duty-free for last-minute gifts including Kit Kat flavors, sake, and Japanese cosmetics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, spend the afternoon at a nearby attraction or head to the airport early to enjoy the extensive duty-free shopping and dining options. Tokyo's airports (Narita and Haneda) both have excellent food courts and souvenir shops — Haneda's International Terminal is particularly impressive with its Edo-period themed shopping street.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Japan with wonderful memories of cherry blossoms, cultural adventures, and family experiences. Enjoy a final Japanese meal at the airport — try a bowl of ramen, a sushi set, or a tonkatsu meal before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — take your time and enjoy the beachfront setting one last time.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or at the airport — try a conveyor belt sushi bar or a simple udon noodle shop for a satisfying and affordable farewell meal (¥800–¥1,500 per person).
meals.dinner: Airport dinner before departure — splurge slightly on a proper sit-down Japanese meal at one of the airport's better restaurants. Budget ¥2,500–¥4,000 per adult for a memorable final meal.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in, security, and immigration at Narita or Haneda. Claim any tax refunds (consumption tax) at the airport tax refund counter before passing through customs — keep all receipts from tax-free shopping. IC cards (Suica/Pasmo) can be returned at airport service counters for a refund of remaining balance minus a small handling fee.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the magical hanami (flower viewing) tradition under Kyoto's most famous weeping cherry tree. Join locals for picnics beneath thousands of blooming sakura trees, enjoy street food stalls, and witness traditional lantern-lit evening viewing. A perfect family cultural immersion that captures the heart of Japanese spring.

experiences.name: Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Explore a mesmerizing world of immersive, interactive digital art installations spread across multiple rooms. Children and adults alike are captivated by the flowing light displays, interactive projections, and dreamlike environments. A uniquely Japanese fusion of technology and art that the whole family will remember.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through Tokyo's legendary outer market sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), grilled scallops, matcha sweets, and street snacks. Engage with friendly vendors, learn about Japanese food culture, and enjoy a hands-on culinary adventure that introduces the whole family to authentic Japanese flavors.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Walk through the iconic towering bamboo forest of Arashiyama, then hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely. Kids will love hand-feeding the monkeys while parents enjoy panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a rickshaw ride along the scenic Oi River for a full cultural and nature experience.

experiences.name: Traditional Samurai and Ninja Experience
experiences.description: Dress the whole family in authentic samurai armor or ninja costumes and learn basic sword techniques and ninja skills from trained instructors. This hands-on cultural workshop offers a thrilling and educational window into feudal Japanese history. Children especially love the ninja throwing star and stealth training activities.
experiences.location: Samurai Kembu Theater, Higashiyama district, Kyoto

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tokyo/Osaka International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer (pre-arranged limousine or black car service) will whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon check-in, enjoy a welcome amenity — chilled sake, seasonal wagashi sweets, and a warm oshibori towel — prepared by the concierge team. Settle into your beachfront suite and unwind.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight
meals.dinner: Light in-room dining upon arrival: a curated bento box featuring seasonal Japanese ingredients, miso soup, and a glass of premium Junmai Daiginjo sake, arranged in advance by the resort concierge.

day_by_day.notes: Request the concierge to prepare a next-day briefing packet and confirm all upcoming reservations. Keep the evening light to combat jet lag. The resort's 24-hour butler service is available for any needs throughout the night.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely late breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant overlooking the beachfront. Afterward, take a gentle orientation stroll along the resort grounds and nearby coastal promenade to acclimate to Japan's atmosphere and time zone.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby cultural landmark or scenic garden (coordinated by the resort concierge based on proximity). Explore a traditional Japanese garden with manicured bonsai, stone lanterns, and koi ponds — a serene and low-energy introduction to Japanese aesthetics. Consider a private guided tour arranged by the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a welcome dinner at the resort's top-tier kaiseki restaurant. Kaiseki is Japan's haute cuisine — a multi-course seasonal tasting menu featuring artistic presentations of the finest local ingredients. Pair with a curated sake flight selected by the in-house sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast featuring freshly made tamagoyaki, grilled fish, miso soup, rice, and a selection of Western options — served with panoramic ocean views.
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort: wagyu beef sliders, edamame, cold soba noodles, and fresh seasonal fruit.
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant — 10-course seasonal tasting menu with optional sake or wine pairing (approx. ¥25,000–¥35,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest-and-acclimatization day. Avoid over-scheduling to ensure the family is energized for the full itinerary ahead. Ask the concierge to confirm all Kyoto and Tokyo excursion bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private chartered vehicle or luxury shinkansen (bullet train) to Kyoto. Upon arrival, head directly to Maruyama Park for the Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. Mid-April is the tail end of cherry blossom season — Kyoto's famous weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) in Maruyama Park is a breathtaking centerpiece. Enjoy a private guided hanami picnic under the blossoms with a premium bento prepared by your hotel's culinary team.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Higashiyama district on foot — stroll the cobblestone lanes of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka, browse artisan shops selling lacquerware, ceramics, and handcrafted souvenirs. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple for panoramic views over Kyoto framed by late-blooming cherry trees.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a private traditional tea ceremony in a historic Kyoto machiya (townhouse) tea room, guided by a certified tea master. Afterward, dinner at a renowned Kyoto kaiseki restaurant in the Gion district.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — Japanese set with grilled salmon, pickles, and green tea.
meals.lunch: Premium hanami bento picnic in Maruyama Park — featuring seasonal chirashi sushi, pickled vegetables, wagashi, and matcha — curated by a Kyoto caterer.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Kikunoi Honten or equivalent Michelin-starred Kyoto kaiseki restaurant in Gion (reservation essential, approx. ¥30,000+ per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book Maruyama Park hanami picnic catering and Kiyomizudera entry in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Higashiyama's stone-paved lanes. A private guide for Kyoto is highly recommended for families to enrich the cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Kyoto. Morning visit to Arashiyama — walk through the iconic Bamboo Grove, where towering green stalks create an otherworldly corridor of light and shadow. The experience is most magical early in the morning before crowds arrive. Arrange a private rickshaw (jinrikisha) ride through the Arashiyama district for a premium, family-friendly way to see the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park in Arashiyama — a family favorite where Japanese macaque monkeys roam freely with stunning views of Kyoto below. Afterward, visit Tenryuji Temple's UNESCO-listed garden, then cross the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge. Optional: traditional cormorant fishing boat cruise on the Oi River (seasonal, check availability).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort or stay overnight at a luxury Kyoto ryokan (traditional inn) such as Tawaraya or Hoshinoya Kyoto for a fully immersive cultural night — featuring private onsen baths, yukata robes, and an in-room kaiseki dinner served by a personal attendant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or hotel before departure — Japanese set meal.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Shoraian, a scenic riverside restaurant in Arashiyama known for tofu cuisine and garden views (approx. ¥5,000–¥10,000 per person).
meals.dinner: In-room kaiseki dinner at Tawaraya Ryokan or Hoshinoya Kyoto — a multi-course feast served in your private tatami suite (approx. ¥40,000+ per person).

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Arashiyama Bamboo Grove by 7:00–8:00 AM to avoid peak crowds. Pre-book the rickshaw and monkey park tickets. If staying at a ryokan overnight, pack an overnight bag — the full ryokan experience is transformative for families and highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Samurai and Ninja Experience — dress the entire family in authentic samurai armor or ninja costumes at a premier Kyoto experience center. Participate in a guided session learning basic sword techniques (kenjutsu), ninja shuriken throwing, and the history and philosophy of the samurai code (bushido). This is one of the most memorable and engaging family activities available in Japan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Nijo Castle — a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring the famous 'nightingale floors' (designed to chirp underfoot to detect intruders) and stunning Edo-period painted sliding doors. Explore the ornate Ninomaru Palace with a private guide. Afterward, browse the Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') for premium food tastings — pickled vegetables, fresh mochi, skewered tofu, and seasonal delicacies.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Maiko (apprentice geisha) dinner performance in a Gion ochaya (teahouse) — a rare, exclusive cultural experience where a maiko performs traditional dances, plays the shamisen, and engages guests in traditional games. Return to resort or ryokan.

meals.breakfast: Ryokan breakfast (if staying overnight) — traditional Japanese morning meal with grilled fish, tofu, pickles, rice, and miso soup.
meals.lunch: Tastings at Nishiki Market followed by a seated lunch at a premium obanzai (Kyoto home-style cuisine) restaurant nearby.
meals.dinner: Private Maiko dinner at a Gion teahouse — multi-course Japanese cuisine with sake and cultural performance (approx. ¥50,000–¥80,000 per group; advance reservation through specialist concierge required).

day_by_day.notes: The Maiko dinner experience requires booking weeks or months in advance through a specialist Kyoto concierge or luxury travel agency — confirm this before the trip. The Samurai/Ninja experience should also be pre-booked for the family group.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Private transfer or luxury shinkansen from Kyoto to Tokyo (approx. 2 hours 15 minutes on the Nozomi). Enjoy the journey — reserve a Green Car (first class) for maximum comfort and enjoy ekiben (premium station bento boxes) purchased at Kyoto Station before boarding.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Tokyo and check into a luxury Tokyo hotel for a one-night stay (e.g., The Peninsula Tokyo, Aman Tokyo, or Park Hyatt Tokyo). After settling in, visit Teamlab Borderless Digital Art Museum — an awe-inspiring, fully immersive digital art world where light, sound, and imagery blend seamlessly across multiple rooms. This experience is equally magical for adults and children and represents the cutting edge of contemporary Japanese art.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Tokyo's upscale Marunouchi or Roppongi district. Enjoy panoramic city views from a rooftop or high-floor fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast at Kyoto ryokan or hotel before checkout.
meals.lunch: Premium ekiben (station bento) on the shinkansen — choose from Kyoto Station's curated selection of regional specialty boxes.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Joël Robuchon Tokyo (Ebisu) or Sukiyabashi Jiro (Ginza) — two of Tokyo's most iconic fine-dining establishments. Alternatively, enjoy teppanyaki wagyu at Ukai-tei Ginza (reservation essential, approx. ¥30,000–¥50,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book Teamlab Borderless tickets online in advance — timed entry slots sell out quickly, especially on weekends. The museum is best experienced with 2–3 hours allocated. Confirm Tokyo hotel reservations and arrange luggage forwarding (takkyubin service) if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — wander through Tokyo's legendary market sampling the freshest sushi, tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), fresh seafood skewers, and seasonal Japanese street food. Arrive by 7:00–8:00 AM for the best selection and atmosphere. A private guide will lead the family through the market's best stalls and hidden gems.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Imperial Palace East Gardens — a serene, beautifully maintained public garden in the heart of Tokyo with late cherry blossoms and traditional Japanese landscaping. Afterward, visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum (or Tokyo National Museum in Ueno) for a deep dive into Japanese history, samurai artifacts, and traditional culture — highly engaging for families.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Tokyo from above: visit the Tokyo Skytree observation deck at sunset for panoramic views of the city stretching to Mount Fuji on clear days. Follow with dinner in the Asakusa district — one of Tokyo's most atmospheric old-town neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Street food breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh tuna sashimi, tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, and matcha soft-serve ice cream.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium sushi counter near Ginza — omakase sushi lunch (chef's selection) at a Michelin-recognized restaurant (approx. ¥15,000–¥25,000 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Asakusa Imahan — a historic sukiyaki and shabu-shabu restaurant renowned for premium wagyu beef, established in 1895 (approx. ¥15,000–¥20,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji Outer Market is best experienced early — plan to arrive no later than 8:00 AM. Wear comfortable shoes and be prepared for narrow, busy lanes. Tokyo Skytree sunset views are spectacular but book priority access tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko or Hakone (choose based on family preference and weather). Hakone Option: Travel by Romancecar luxury train to Hakone. Visit the Open Air Museum (Chokoku no Mori) — an extraordinary outdoor sculpture park blending art with nature, beloved by families. Enjoy views of Mount Fuji across Lake Ashi on a sightseeing cruise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hakone: Ride the Hakone Ropeway over volcanic Owakudani valley with sulfuric steam vents and dramatic mountain scenery. Try the famous black eggs (kuro-tamago) hard-boiled in volcanic hot springs — legend says each egg adds seven years to your life. Check into a premium Hakone ryokan (e.g., Gora Kadan or Hakone Ginyu) for an overnight onsen experience.
day_by_day.evening: Private open-air onsen (rotenburo) bath at the ryokan with views of Mount Fuji or the surrounding forested mountains. Followed by a multi-course kaiseki dinner in your private suite or the ryokan's dining room.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast at the Tokyo hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Hakone Open Air Museum's restaurant or a local Hakone soba restaurant — fresh mountain soba with seasonal toppings.
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at Gora Kadan or Hakone Ginyu ryokan — a seasonal multi-course feast featuring local mountain vegetables, fresh river fish, and premium wagyu (included in ryokan package, approx. ¥60,000–¥100,000 per couple including accommodation).

day_by_day.notes: Mount Fuji visibility is weather-dependent — the concierge can advise on the best viewing days. Book the Hakone ryokan well in advance as premium rooms sell out months ahead. The onsen experience is a must-do for families — many ryokans offer private family bath options.

day_by_day.morning: Wake early at the Hakone ryokan for a private sunrise onsen soak. Enjoy the full traditional ryokan breakfast — an elaborate spread of grilled fish, tofu, pickles, miso soup, and rice served in your room. Take a final morning stroll through the ryokan's Japanese garden before checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Tokyo by Romancecar. Spend the afternoon in Harajuku and Omotesando — Tokyo's most fashionable and architecturally stunning shopping district. Visit the Omotesando Hills complex for luxury Japanese and international brands. Explore Takeshita Street for quirky, colorful Japanese pop culture — a fun contrast for families. Visit the Meiji Shrine nearby for a peaceful forest walk and a glimpse of Shinto ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Final Tokyo evening: Enjoy a premium dinner in Shinjuku or Shibuya with a view of the famous Shibuya Crossing — the world's busiest pedestrian intersection. Afterward, explore the neon-lit streets of Shinjuku's entertainment district for dessert and nightcap at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Full traditional ryokan breakfast in-room at Hakone — a lavish Japanese morning spread.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium tempura restaurant in Omotesando — Kondo Tempura (Ginza) or equivalent, featuring seasonal vegetable and seafood tempura (approx. ¥15,000 per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at New York Bar, Park Hyatt Tokyo (Shinjuku) — iconic fine-dining with live jazz and sweeping city views, made famous by 'Lost in Translation' (approx. ¥20,000–¥30,000 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Meiji Shrine is free to enter and a wonderful cultural contrast to the surrounding fashion district. Shibuya Crossing is best viewed from above — book a window table at Shibuya Sky observation deck or a nearby restaurant for the full effect.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan — check out of the Tokyo hotel. Depending on departure time, enjoy a leisurely last breakfast and a final stroll through the hotel's neighborhood. Visit a nearby artisan shop or department store basement food hall (depachika) — Tokyo's department store basement food halls are world-class, stocking the finest Japanese confections, teas, and gourmet gifts perfect for souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to the airport. Allow ample time for Tokyo's traffic and airport procedures. At the airport, explore the premium duty-free and artisan retail zones — Narita and Haneda both offer excellent selections of Japanese whisky, sake, matcha products, and high-end crafts. Enjoy a final meal at one of the airport's top-rated restaurants before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Board departure flight. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through Japan's most iconic cultural, culinary, and natural treasures.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Tokyo hotel — choose between a Japanese set or Western buffet. Savor a final cup of premium Japanese green tea.
meals.lunch: Depachika gourmet lunch — assemble a premium picnic from the department store basement food hall: premium onigiri, sushi rolls, wagashi sweets, and fresh juice.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the airport — Narita's Sushi Saito outpost or Haneda's premium dining floor offers exceptional last meals; alternatively, enjoy a bento from a premium airport vendor on board.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase premium Japanese souvenirs at the depachika or airport: Yojiya cosmetics, Toraya wagashi, Mariage Frères Japanese teas, Nikka or Suntory whisky, and regional craft items. Confirm airport transfer timing with the hotel concierge the night before. Allow at least 3 hours before an international departure from Narita or Haneda.
